newsitem.title: USA: 3M to sell advertising unit for $1 billion.
newsitem.headline: 3M to sell advertising unit for $1 billion.

text.p: Minnesota Mining & Manufacturing Co. said on Thursday it has agreed to sell National Advertising Co., its outdoor and mall advertising company, to Outdoor Systems Inc. for $1 billion.
In a news release, 3M said it was selling the unit to focus on its core businesses and because it felt substantial investment would be needed in the outdoor advertising industry.
The company also suggested that layoffs at the advertising unit might occur but it wasn't specific.

"The outdoor advertising industry has changed significantly in recent years, and we recognise that substantial investments would be required to maintain market leadership," said Ray Richelsen, 3M group vice president.
"3M is focusing on opportunities for growth where our innovation and core technologies give us a competitive advantage on a worldwide basis," he said.
National Advertising, based in Bedford Park, Ill., employs about 530 people across the United States.
Richelsen said the company's immediate focus will be on a successful transition, "including those employees whose services may be not required by the purchaser."
3M is a diversified manufacturing company with 1996 sales of $14.2 billion.
The sale is subject to government approval, the company said.
3M's stock rose 12.5 cents to $87.125 early on the New York Stock Exchange.
